Looking at my situation: I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain. This flat land with access to groundwater irrigation has been in my family's wheat-maize rotation for generations. My father grew wheat and maize, and so did his father. I have about 8 mu of farmland.

I'm not going to experiment. The winter wheat – summer maize rotation is what works here. The government sets a floor price for wheat, the village supply station stocks the inputs I need, and I know this system. Last year's wheat yielded around 440 kg/mu which I was satisfied with.

For wheat, I'll sow in mid-October after rotary tillage to break up the maize stubble. I'll use Aikang 58 — the agricultural technician at the township station pushed it last year and my neighbor got decent results. I'll put down compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress with urea at jointing. I'll irrigate at overwintering, jointing, and grain-filling — three times. I'll spray herbicide in late autumn and a fungicide before heading.

For summer maize, I'll direct-seed Zhengdan 958 right after wheat harvest in June — no ploughing, just go straight in. Rain during summer usually covers most of the water need. I might irrigate once around tasseling if it's dry. Herbicide right after emergence, and watch for corn borer around mid-summer.
